plain_english_policy:
This document outlines the rules for a firefighter's retirement and disability fund. Here are the key points in simple terms:

**Retirement Benefits (Based on Service Time):**
*   **Less than 48 months:** No specific benefit amount is listed here, but it implies eligibility might be different.
*   **At least 48 to less than 59 months:** You get $144 per month.
*   **60 months or more:** You get $180 per month.

**Disability Benefits & Rules:**
*   If you are disabled for over 24 months, you can retire and get benefits if you meet the requirements in Section 10 (which likely covers age/service).
*   **Inactive Status:** If you draw disability benefits for 24 straight months but don't go back to work:
    *   Your account goes "inactive" for up to 36 months.
    *   You get no money or special rights during this time.
    *   **If you return within 36 months:** You can come back as a firefighter, pay dues, and your past service years are restored (counted again).
    *   **If you don't return after 36 months:** Your account is closed forever. No more rights or benefits.
*   **Closed Account Consequence:** If your account was closed because of the rule above and you try to join again later, you lose all credit for past service up until it was closed. You start fresh as a new member.

**Death Benefits (Section 12):**
*   The board promises to pay $2,500 to your chosen beneficiary if you die while still an active firefighter (after paying off any debts owed to the fund).
*   **Killed in Duty:** If you are killed on duty, your family gets:
    *   All membership fees you paid back.
    *   The $2,500 death benefit mentioned above. These two payments add together.

**Fund Management & Changes (Sections 13-16):**
*   **Actuary:** An expert accountant checks the fund every three years to make sure it has enough money. They might suggest changing payment amounts up or down for everyone based on how well the fund is doing.
*   **No Liability Guarantee:** The government, board, or anyone else isn't personally responsible if payments need to be cut due to financial problems (pro rata reduction).
*   **Withdrawal:** You can quit and get 90% of what you paid in. But once you take this money:
    *   You lose all rights.
    *   If you want to join again, you must start as a brand new member.
    *   However, if you stop being a firefighter but don't take the cash yet (for up to 36 months), and then come back as a firefighter within that time, your old service years are kept. After 36 months without returning, your account closes and fees are refunded (service lost).
*   **Reports:** The executive director reports money status twice a year. An independent auditor checks everything once a year for the state legislature.

**Important Legal Notes:**
*   **No Vested Rights:** Rules can change by the Legislature in the future, except if you've already been getting retirement benefits for 2 years (then your service time is locked in unless there was fraud).
*   **Protected Money:** Your annuity/benefits cannot be taken away to pay debts or court judgments against you.
*   **Other Plans:** This fund doesn't replace other pensions. You can join this one even if you are part of another retirement system.
policy_direction_if_enacted: This act establishes a specific retirement and disability benefit structure for firefighters, defining payment tiers based on service length ($144/month vs $180/month), outlining strict rules regarding returning to duty after disability (36-month window to restore status or lose benefits permanently), setting death benefits at $2,500 plus fee refunds for line-of-duty deaths, and explicitly stating that these funds are protected from creditors but subject to future legislative changes unless a member has received benefits for two years.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill appears to be sponsored by the Senate (McDowell Lee, Secretary) and passed/amended through both chambers. The text provided is the final certified version.
evidence_quotes: One hundred forty-four dollars ($144) per calendar month if his or her qualified service is at least 48 months and not more than 59 months.
One hundred eighty dollars ($180) per calendar month if his or her qualified service is 60 months or more.
Any member disabled as defined in this section for a period of more than 24 calendar months shall be eligible for retirement benefits under this act if he or she meets the requirements of Section 10.
review_reason: The text provided is clear, complete legal language without obvious errors requiring human intervention.
